chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who manumitted his slave on condition that the inheritance belongs to him. He said, 'This was referred to Ali (peace be upon him), who annulled his condition, saying, 'The condition of God is prior to your condition.'

key_terms.كَاتَبَ: He entered into a contract of manumission (mukatabah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a master's condition that he inherits from his mukatab slave?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the chain of Jamil, clarifies the ruling of the mukatab by linking it to the precedent of Imam Ali (AS), thereby establishing a continuous jurisprudential lineage. It asserts that the divine right of inheritance supersedes contractual stipulations, reflecting the Shia principle that 'the condition of God is prior to your condition.' This ruling ensures that the mukatab’s estate is not arbitrarily withheld by the master, preserving the slave’s financial autonomy upon manumission or death.
